title: A Tight Correlation between Millimeter and X-Ray Emission in Accreting Massive Black Holes from <100 mas Resolution ALMA Observations
question: What is the relation between nuclear 100 GHz millimeter continuum emission and X-ray emission in nearby hard X-ray selected radio-quiet AGN at <100 mas resolution, and can 100 GHz emission be used to probe AGN accretion and column density?

evidence.loc: Sample
evidence.quote: Our sample was drawn from the Swift/BAT 70-month catalog (cite: Baumgartner:2013uq).

what.value: Broad-band (0.3-150 keV) X-ray fluxes and column densities

evidence.loc: Sample
evidence.quote: We use the X-ray fluxes and column densities obtained by (cite: Ricci:2017if) through broad-band (0.3–150 keV) X-ray spectral analysis.

evidence.loc: Sample

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Band 3 continuum observations and extract nuclear 100 GHz fluxes
recipe.method: Calibrate and image Band 3 data with the ALMA pipeline in CASA using Briggs weighting (robust = 0.5), create primary-beam corrected aggregated continuum maps, and measure the peak flux for each source (using the brighter component in dual-source systems and a 3-sigma upper limit for the non-detection).
assumptions: Brighter nuclear source used for dual systems NGC 3281 and NGC 4941

recipe.goal: Derive intrinsic X-ray luminosities, 2-10 keV fluxes/luminosities, bolometric luminosities, and Eddington ratios
recipe.method: Combine literature broad-band X-ray measurements with new NuSTAR spectral analysis for eight Compton-thick sources, calculate luminosities using BASS DR2 distances, convert 14-150 keV to 2-10 keV assuming a power-law with photon index 1.8, and compute bolometric luminosities and Eddington ratios.
assumptions: Cosmological parameters H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7
Pure power-law X-ray spectrum with photon index Gamma = 1.8

recipe.goal: Fit correlations between 100 GHz and X-ray luminosities and fluxes, and test dependence on AGN/host parameters
recipe.method: Fit linear relations to the logarithms of 100 GHz and X-ray (14-150 keV and 2-10 keV) luminosities and fluxes using a standard linear least-squares method, compute median luminosity ratios, and check for correlations with column density, Eddington ratio, black hole mass, and star formation rate.

recipe.goal: Calibrate relation between column density and observed 2-10 keV to 100 GHz flux ratio and compare with torus model
recipe.method: Fit a linear relation between log(N_H) and log(F_2-10keV^obs / F_100GHz) in the range log(N_H) = 22-24.5, and compare against theoretical predictions from the REFLEX RXTORUSD dusty torus X-ray model.
key_parameters: Gamma = 1.8, E_C = 200 keV, torus covering factor = 70%, f_scatt = 1.1%
assumptions: Constant log(F_2-10keV^obs / F_100GHz) = 2.7 for log(N_H / cm^-2) >= 24.5

evidence.loc: Abstract
evidence.quote: We find an extremely high detection rate (25/26 or $94^{+3}_{-6}\%$), which shows that nuclear emission at mm-wavelengths is nearly ubiquitous in accreting SMBHs.

evidence.loc: ALMA data reduction
evidence.quote: In two cases (NGC 3281 and NGC 4941) ALMA detected two nuclear sources (per galaxy), separated by $\sim 0.3\ensuremath{''}$. In both cases, the fluxes of the two nuclear sources were almost identical, with flux ratios of $1.07$ and $1.11$ for NGC 4941 and NGC 3281, respectively.

score_reason: The ALMA data are processed with exact stated versions of CASA (6.1.1.15) and the ALMA pipeline (2020.1.0.40) using standard robust=0.5 aggregated continuum maps, peak flux extraction is straightforward, and all 26 target fluxes/luminosities are tabulated in Table 1, allowing direct reproduction of the main correlation fits.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA dataset (2019.1.01230.S) reduced with the standard ALMA pipeline, simple peak-flux extraction on aggregated continuum maps, tabulated multi-wavelength data in Table 1, and clear numeric answer keys (detection fraction and linear regression slopes/intercepts/scatter).
